arxiv-2011-06896.title: CentiTrack: Towards Centimeter-Level Passive Gesture Tracking with Commodity WiFi
arxiv-2011-06896.creator: Zijun Han, Zhaoming Lu, Xiangming Wen, Wei Zheng, Jingbo Zhao, Lingchao Guo
arxiv-2011-06896.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Zijun Han, Zhaoming Lu, Xiangming Wen, Wei Zheng, Jingbo Zhao, Lingchao Guo. Gesture awareness plays a crucial role in promoting human-computer interface. Previous works either depend on customized hardware or need a priori learning of wireless signal patterns, facing downsides in terms of the privacy concern, availability and reliability. In this paper, we propose CentiTrack, the first centimeter-level passive gesture tracking system that works with only three commodity WiFi devices, without any extra hardware modifications or wearable sensors.

arxiv-2305-07932.title: Novel approach for computing gradients of physical observables Preprint: DESY 22-
arxiv-2305-07932.creator: Simone Bacchio
arxiv-2305-07932.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Simone Bacchio. We show that an infinitesimal step of gradient flow can be used for defining a novel approach for computing gradients of physical observables with respect to action parameters. Compared to the commonly used perturbative expansion, this approach does not require calculating any disconnected contribution or vacuum expectation value and can provide results up to three orders of magnitudes more precise.

arxiv-2310-20195.title: Generating Continuations in Multilingual Idiomatic Contexts
arxiv-2310-20195.creator: Rhitabrat Pokharel, Ameeta Agrawal
arxiv-2310-20195.description: Abstract The ability to process idiomatic or literal multiword expressions is a crucial aspect of understanding and generating any language. The task of generating contextually relevant continuations for narratives containing idiomatic (or literal) expressions can allow us to test the ability of generative language models (LMs) in understanding nuanced language containing non-compositional figurative text.

arxiv-2402-01105.title: A Survey for Foundation Models in Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2402-01105.creator: Haoxiang Gao, Zhongruo Wang, Yaqian Li, Kaiwen Long, Ming Yang, Yiqing Shen
arxiv-2402-01105.description: Abstract The advent of foundation models has revolutionized the fields of natural language processing and computer vision, paving the way for their application in autonomous driving (AD). This survey presents a comprehensive review of more than 40 research papers, demonstrating the role of foundation models in enhancing AD.

arxiv-2406-04348.title: Gaining Insights into Group-Level Course Difficulty via Differential Course Functioning
arxiv-2406-04348.creator: Frederik Baucks, Robin Schmucker, Conrad Borchers, Zachary A. Pardos, Laurenz Wiskott
arxiv-2406-04348.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Frederik Baucks, Robin Schmucker, Conrad Borchers, Zachary A. Pardos, Laurenz Wiskott. Curriculum Analytics (CA) studies curriculum structure and student data to ensure the quality of educational programs. One desirable property of courses within curricula is that they are not unexpectedly more difficult for students of different backgrounds. While prior work points to likely variations in course difficulty across student groups, robust methodologies for capturing such variations are scarce, and existing approaches do not adequately decouple course-specific difficulty from students’ general performance levels.

arxiv-2408-06559.title: Asymptotic perpendicular transport in low-beta collisionless plasma
arxiv-2408-06559.creator: Jack Coughlin, Jingwei Hu, Uri Shumlak
arxiv-2408-06559.description: Abstract Kinetic physics, including finite Larmor radius (FLR) effects, are known to affect the physics of magnetized plasma phenomena such as the Kelvin-Helmholtz and Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities. Accurately incorporating FLR effects into fluid simulations requires moment closures for the heat flux and stress tensor, including the gyroviscous stress in collisionless magnetized plasmas.

arxiv-2505-23239.creator: Lingkai Meng, Yu Shao, Long Yuan, Longbin Lai, Peng Cheng, Wenyuan Yu, Wenjie Zhang, Xuemin Lin, Jingren Zhou
arxiv-2505-23239.description: Abstract . Usability evaluation is critical to the impact and adoption of open source software (OSS), yet traditional methods relying on human evaluators suffer from high costs and limited scalability. To address these limitations, we introduce 𝖮𝖲𝖲 \mathsf{OSS} - 𝖴𝖠𝗀𝖾𝗇𝗍 \mathsf{UAgent} , an automated, configurable, and interactive agent-based usability evaluation framework specifically designed for open source software.

arxiv-2509-08607.title: MasconCube: Fast and Accurate Gravity Modeling with an Explicit Representation
arxiv-2509-08607.creator: Pietro Fanti 1, Dario Izzo 1 \cor
arxiv-2509-08607.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pietro Fanti 1, Dario Izzo 1 \cor. The geodesy of irregularly shaped small bodies presents fundamental challenges for gravitational field modeling, particularly as deep space exploration missions increasingly target asteroids and comets. Traditional approaches suffer from critical limitations: spherical harmonics diverge within the Brillouin sphere where spacecraft typically operate, polyhedral models assume unrealistic homogeneous density distributions, and existing machine learning methods like GeodesyNets and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN-GM) require extensive computational resources and training time.

arxiv-2601-10968.title: Radiative cooling effects on plasmoid formation in black hole accretion flows with multiple magnetic loops
arxiv-2601-10968.creator: Jing-Ze Xia ˙, Hong-Xuan Jiang ˙, Yosuke Mizuno ˙, Antonios Nathanail, Christian M. Fromm
arxiv-2601-10968.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jing-Ze Xia ˙, Hong-Xuan Jiang ˙, Yosuke Mizuno ˙, Antonios Nathanail, Christian M. Fromm. We investigate the physics of black hole accretion flows, particularly focusing on phenomena like magnetic reconnection and plasmoid formation, which are believed to be responsible for energetic events such as flares observed from astrophysical black holes. We aim to understand the influence of radiative cooling on plasmoid formation within black hole accretion flows that are threaded by multi-loop magnetic field configurations.

pmc-11625681.title: Rasmussen aneurysm in a patient with pulmonary tuberculosis
pmc-11625681.creator: Salman Ahmed Malik, Allahdad Khan, Humaira Siddique, Kamran Ahmed Malik, Muhammad Usman, Mohamed Antar
pmc-11625681.description: Key messageRasmussen aneurysm is a rare complication of tuberculosis, where a pulmonary artery adjacent to a tuberculous cavity aneurysm may lead to life threatening hemoptysis. Sudden or severe hemoptysis is an emergency condition in TB patients who need prompt recognition and intervention, often through endovascular embolization, to prevent fatal outcomes.

pmc-12483136.description: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer, requires early and accurate detection to optimize clinical management. pmc-12646304.title: Time-of-day modulation in mosquito response persistence to carbon dioxide is controlled by Pigment-Dispersing Factor
pmc-12646304.creator: Linhan Dong, Richard Hormigo, Jord M. Barnett, Chloe Greppi, Laura B. Duvall
pmc-12646304.description: SignificanceMosquitoes use rhythmic sensory responses to find human hosts, but the role of circadian rhythms in this behavior is not well understood. Using an automated assay, we show that Aedes aegypti mosquitoes’ responses to CO2, a critical host cue, vary with time of day. While activation is stable during daylight, persistence peaks at dawn and dusk, matching natural biting times.
